info.title: sparkbox control API
info.description:
The sparkbox control plane, owner-scoped.

This API mirrors the `ssh ctl@example.com …` command surface: the two share one implementation (`internal/ctlops`), so ownership rules, timeout budgets and validation are identical whichever door you come through.

**Authentication.** Every `/v1` endpoint needs an edge session token. Mint one over SSH:

    TOKEN=$(ssh ctl@example.com session-token | tr -d '\r\n')

and send it as `Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN`. Browsers signed in at `https://login.example.com` already carry the same value in the `spark_session` cookie, which is scoped to the whole zone.

**Authorization is ownership.** You see and act on your own sandboxes, snapshots, schedules and keys. Someone else's resource answers exactly like one that does not exist — a 404 with the same body — so the API never confirms which names are taken.

**Long operations.** Pausing writes a full guest memory snapshot; archiving compresses and uploads a 25 GB disk. Those calls start a job, wait ten seconds for it, and answer `200`/`201` if it finished or `202` with a job to poll if it did not. Send `Prefer: respond-async` to skip the wait, or `Prefer: wait=30` to widen it. Retrying the same call while its job runs returns the *same* job rather than starting a second one.

**Errors** from `/v1` handlers are always `{"error": {"kind", "op", "code", "message", …}}`. Switch on `code`: it is a stable token that never changes once shipped. `message` is a complete sentence fit to show a user. The two refusals the *auth gate* raises before a handler runs are the exceptions and are `text/plain`: `401` with no valid session, and `403` on a state-changing call made with the cookie alone and no first-party proof (see `sessionCookie`).

tags.description: The specification and the docs page. Unauthenticated, so you can read how to get a token before you have one.

get.description: A bare visit lands on /docs rather than a 404.
A self-contained HTML page that renders this specification client-side. No CDN, no external fetch.
The canonical specification, with every example host rewritten to this host's zone. A test pins it to the router: an endpoint that is not described here does not exist, and vice versa.
The same bytes as /openapi.json, re-emitted in key order.
Archiving needs object storage, snapshots need a driver that supports them, scheduling and tagging need their stores. Read this instead of discovering a 501 by trying.
Mirrors `ssh ctl@example.com whoami`. `key_fp` is empty here: an HTTP request carries no SSH key.
Every sandbox you own, in creation order. Other owners' sandboxes are not listed and not counted.

post.description:
The REST form of `ssh new@example.com`. Omit `name` and the platform generates an adjective-noun one.

Tags are stamped **before** the VM is created, because creation fires the secret-environment push asynchronously and the tags decide its contents. If creation fails, the tag rows are rolled back.

Unlike the SSH door, there is no way to pass a command: named fields have no ambiguity to resolve.

409.description: That name is taken or reserved.

get.description: Does not resume a paused sandbox — reading is never a side effect.

delete.description: Irreversible. Cascades to the sandbox's web routes, schedules, tags, front-door DNS record and, if it was archived, the stored object.

post.description: Writes the guest's full memory snapshot and frees its RAM. Resuming restores the running processes exactly. Budget: 3 minutes.
Starts a paused sandbox from its memory snapshot. If the sandbox was archived, this also downloads and decompresses its disk first, which is why the budget is 15 minutes.

post.summary: Archive a sandbox to object storage
post.description: Checks the filesystem, zeroes free space, compresses the disk and uploads it, then frees the host disk entirely. Resuming restores it. Needs object storage: hosts without it answer 501. Budget: 15 minutes, so this almost always returns 202.

Grow-only. The sandbox is paused, its memory snapshot is **discarded**, the filesystem is checked and grown, and the guest cold-boots — so anything running inside dies. Send `size` ("25G", "512M", or a bare number meaning GB) or `size_mb`. Budget: 10 minutes.
Discards the memory snapshot and boots the guest fresh. Running processes die; the disk is untouched.
Moves the sandbox's default web route and front-door DNS record with it. The old hostname stops resolving.

409.description: The new name is taken or reserved.

post.summary: Exempt a sandbox from the idle reaper
post.description: Sets the always-on flag and nothing else. `ssh ctl@example.com pin` also resumes the sandbox; here the two are separate calls, so there is no half-succeeded state to interpret. Resume afterwards if you want it running now.
Clears the always-on flag. The sandbox is paused again once it has been idle for the host's idle timeout.

get.description: Tags select which of your secrets are pushed into the guest's environment.

put.description: Replaces the whole set; `[]` clears it. Tags are lowercased, de-duplicated and sorted, and at most 32 are kept. The guest's secret environment is re-pushed immediately rather than at the next resume.

get.description: Every forwarded hostname pointing at this sandbox, with the port it forwards to and whether it is reachable without signing in.

put.summary: Make a sandbox public or private
put.description: Flips **every** route of the sandbox together, matching `ssh ctl@example.com share`. `private` requires a signed-in owner (or operator); `public` serves anyone.

200.description: The routes as stored, and how many changed.

get.summary: Open a shell over a WebSocket
get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying a PTY inside the sandbox — the same session the page at `https://<name>-xterm.example.com` opens. The sandbox is resumed if it is paused; the ownership check happens first, so this can never wake someone else's VM.

**Framing.** Terminal bytes travel in **binary** frames in both directions, unmodified: PTY output splits multi-byte characters across reads, and a text frame would have to be valid UTF-8. Set `binaryType = 'arraybuffer'` on the client.

Control messages are **text** frames carrying JSON:

    {"type":"resize","rows":40,"cols":120}

Send one immediately after connecting and on every resize.

**Close codes.** `4001` the shell exited normally (the value the exe-ssh terminal-over-HTTPS design reserves for the same meaning); `4002` the host hung the session up — a pause, an idle reap, or a redeploy — which is the signal to offer a reconnect; `4003` the sandbox could not be attached to. `1000` is not sent.

**Authentication.** This is a `GET`, so it takes the session cookie a browser sends automatically; a non-browser client sends `Authorization: Bearer`. Because a browser cannot attach a custom header to a handshake, the CSRF gate is replaced by an `Origin` check on the upgrade itself.

101.description: Switching Protocols — the WebSocket is open.

403.description: The handshake carried an `Origin` that is not this host, or no `Origin` and no `Authorization: Bearer`. Answered before the upgrade, so the body is `text/plain`, not the JSON envelope.

426.description: Not a WebSocket handshake — the `Connection`/`Upgrade` headers are missing. `text/plain`.

505.description: The request arrived over HTTP/2, which cannot be hijacked; the terminal needs HTTP/1.1. `text/plain`.

get.description: Snapshots are keyed by owner, so this can only ever show your own.

post.summary: Capture a sandbox as a template
post.description: **Pauses the sandbox.** The managed secret-environment block is stripped from the disk, the guest is paused, and the disk is compacted into a template. Name must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,40}$` and be unique among your snapshots. Budget: 15 minutes.

409.description: You already have a snapshot by that name. There is no overwrite; delete it first.

delete.description: Sandboxes already forked from it are unaffected.

post.summary: Create a sandbox from a snapshot
post.description: A fork is a create with the snapshot as its disk, so it is admitted against the same per-owner running limit and disk pool, and its tags are stamped before it exists for the same reason.

409.description: That sandbox name is taken or reserved.

get.description: `next_run` is absent when the stored spec no longer parses.

post.summary: Run a command on a schedule
post.description: `spec` is a standard 5-field cron expression or one of the descriptors (`@hourly`, `@daily`, `@every 30m`). The host resumes the sandbox when the entry fires, so scheduling against a paused sandbox is normal.

delete.description: Someone else's schedule id answers exactly like one that does not exist.

get.description: Every key that can open an SSH session as you. `current` is never set here — an HTTP request has no session key.

post.description: Takes one `authorized_keys` line; its comment becomes the label. Adding a key you already have is a no-op rather than an error. A key already linked to another account is refused with 409.

409.description: That key is already linked to another account.

delete.description: The fingerprint is a query parameter, not a path segment: it is `SHA256:` plus unpadded base64, whose alphabet includes `/`. Removing your last key is refused — it would lock you out of SSH entirely.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: The key's `SHA256:…` fingerprint, exactly as listed — **percent-encoded**. The base64 alphabet includes `+` and `/`, and a query decoder reads a bare `+` as a space.

post.description: Fetches `https://github.com/<your linked login>.keys` and adds each key. Keys already linked to a different sparkbox account are reported in `skipped` and the import continues. Link a login first with `POST /v1/account/github`.

409.description: No GitHub login is linked yet.

post.description: Proves the link by finding one of your **already registered** keys on `github.com/<login>.keys`. Name which key with `fingerprint` — over SSH the session key is implied, but an HTTP request has none. A fingerprint that is not yours answers 404, so it cannot be used to test whether a key exists.

200.description: Linked; your account as it now stands.

403.description: That key is not listed on the GitHub account.

get.description: Passkeys are enrolled in the browser at `https://login.example.com`; this API is the audit-and-revoke end.

delete.description: Any unique prefix of the id works. An ambiguous prefix answers 409 with the matching ids in `details.matches`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The passkey id, or any unique prefix of it.

409.description: The prefix matches more than one passkey.

get.description: The address the edge sends upstream as `X-Forwarded-Email` when a private route serves your request.

200.description: The stored address, or an empty string.

put.summary: Set or clear your forwarded email address
put.description: An empty string clears it. This is a PUT rather than a DELETE because "no address" is a value the account holds, not the absence of a resource.

post.description: Issues the same credential `ssh ctl@example.com session-token` prints — the one this API authenticates with. Use it to turn a browser session into a scriptable one, or to rotate a script's token before it expires. `ttl` is a Go duration; it defaults to 12h and is silently clamped to 7 days.

201.description: The token. Store it; it cannot be read back.

post.description: The only operator-gated call in this API. Operators may always mint; everyone else may mint up to the host's per-user quota, which is zero by default. Codes are redeemed at `ssh signup@example.com` and last 7 days.

403.description: Not an operator, or the per-user invite quota is spent.

get.summary: List the machines in this fleet
get.description: Operators only. Includes this gateway, which is listed with `local: true` and no fingerprint. A machine that has enrolled itself is `pending` until an operator compares its fingerprint out of band and approves it. On a host that is not a fleet gateway this answers 501.

post.summary: Let an enrolled machine into the fleet
post.description: Operators only. This is the whole trust ceremony: compare the fingerprint from `GET /v1/nodes` against the one the machine printed at boot, then approve. Idempotent — approving an already-approved node re-records who approved it.

delete.summary: Drop a machine from the fleet
delete.description: Operators only. Refused with 409 while the node still holds sandboxes: they live on that machine's disk, so removing the row would not delete them, it would strand them under a name nothing in the fleet claims. Removal revokes the approval rather than banning the key — the machine may enrol again and wait.

409.description: The node still holds sandboxes, or it is this gateway itself. `details.sandboxes` is the count.

get.description: Newest first. Jobs live in memory: a control-plane restart forgets them, because the restart also killed the work they describe. Finished jobs are readable for an hour.
`result` carries whatever the completed operation would have returned inline; `error` carries the failure in the ordinary error shape.

delete.description: Cancels the work's context and waits briefly for it to stop, so the answer usually already reads `canceled`. A job that has already finished is a 409: there is nothing left to cancel, and an archive that completed cannot be un-completed.

bearerAuth.description: An edge session token. Mint one with `ssh ctl@example.com session-token | tr -d '\r\n'` (the channel ends the line CRLF, and a stray carriage return in the header is rejected), or `POST /v1/account/tokens` from an existing session.

sessionCookie.name: spark_session
sessionCookie.description: The same token, as the zone-wide cookie a browser gets from `https://login.example.com`. State-changing calls made with the cookie alone must also prove first-party intent — an `Origin` matching this host, or the header `X-Sparkbox-Console: 1` — because the cookie rides every same-site request. Bearer-authenticated calls need neither.

NodeName.name: name
NodeName.description: The node name, as listed. It is the name the roster holds, not whatever the machine last called itself.

JobID.name: id
JobID.description: The job id, as returned in a 202 or in `href`.

Prefer.name: Prefer
Prefer.description: `respond-async` to get a 202 immediately without waiting; `wait=<seconds>` to change the sync window from its 10-second default (60 maximum). The applied preference is echoed in `Preference-Applied`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: An opaque key of your choosing. The first response is remembered for 24 hours and replayed verbatim (with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`) if the key comes back. Reusing a key with a different request body is a 422; sending it while the first request is still running is a 409. Server errors are never cached, so a 5xx can always be retried with the same key.

Accepted.description: The operation is still running. Poll the job at `Location`.

NotFound.description: No such resource — or it belongs to someone else. The two are deliberately indistinguishable.

Disabled.description: This host has not configured that feature. Check `GET /v1/capabilities` first.

error.message: archiving is not enabled on this host

RunningLimit.description: You are at your per-owner running-sandbox limit. `details.running` lists them.

error.message: you already have 3 running sandboxes (max 3): a, b, c
error.hint: Pause one to free a slot.

HostAtCapacity.description: The host has no RAM budget left. Try again shortly.

DiskPoolFull.description: Your disk pool is full. Archive or delete a sandbox to reclaim space.

Error.description: Every failure has this shape. Switch on `error.code`.

kind.description: The broad class of failure, which fixes the status code.

op.description: The operation that failed — the same string as the operationId.

code.description: A stable machine token. Never localized, never changed once shipped.

message.description: A complete sentence, fit to show a user unedited.

hint.description: What to do about it, when there is something to do.

details.description: Structured facts a client can act on: `running` for a limit, `budget_mb` for capacity, `matches` for an ambiguous passkey prefix.

Capabilities.description: What this host has configured. A false field means those endpoints answer 501.

snapshots.description: The VM driver can capture templates.

tags.description: The secrets store is open, so tags exist.

fleet.description: This host is a gateway other machines can join, so the node endpoints answer. It says nothing about whether any machine has joined.

Sandbox.description: One microVM. Internal topology — its guest address, its host IP — is deliberately not part of this shape.

state.description: `archived` means the disk lives in object storage and a resume must fetch it.

node.description: The machine this sandbox runs on.

unreachable.description: The machine holding this sandbox is not answering the control plane right now. It is very likely still running.

ballooned.description: The guest has given RAM back to the host and will reclaim it on demand.

tags.description: Never null. Selects which secrets reach the guest's environment.

last_active.description: What the idle reaper measures against. Guest CPU and network activity refresh it, not an attached terminal.

terminal_url.description: The browser terminal, when this host serves them.

CreateRequest.description: All fields are optional; an empty body creates a default sandbox with a generated name.

name.description: Omit to get a generated adjective-noun name.

tags.description: Stamped before the VM exists, so the first secret push already has them.

ResizeRequest.description: Send one of the two. `size` is what `ctl resize` accepts; `size_mb` is for callers that already have a number.

size.description: "25G", "512M", or a bare number meaning GB.

size_mb.description: The new size in MiB. Capped at 1 TB.

tags.description: The whole set. Lowercased, de-duplicated and sorted on write.

port.description: The guest port this hostname forwards to.

visibility.description: `private` requires a signed-in owner or operator.

changed.description: How many routes this call flipped. Absent on a read.

from_sandbox.description: The sandbox it was captured from.

sandbox.description: The sandbox to capture. It will be paused.

next_run.description: Absent when the stored spec no longer parses.

last_exit.description: The command's exit status on its last run.

last_error.description: Set when the run could not happen at all, as opposed to running and failing.

handle.description: Immutable: it appears in the OIDC subject claim.

operator.description: True for accounts seeded from the host's users.conf.

subject.description: The `sub` claim this host issues for you.

key_fp.description: The SSH key on this session. Always absent over HTTP.

label.description: The comment from the authorized_keys line.

via.description: How the key arrived: seed, signup, ctl, github-import.

current.description: The key authenticating this session. Never set over HTTP.

login.description: Omit to re-verify the login already linked.

fingerprint.description: Which of YOUR registered keys to prove the link with. It must be listed on github.com/<login>.keys.

imported.description: Genuinely new keys. Re-running the import is free.

skipped.description: Fingerprints already linked to a different account. Never null.

email.description: An empty string means no address is set.

ttl.description: A Go duration. Defaults to 12h, clamped to 168h.

Node.description: One machine in the fleet: the roster row joined to the live link. The machine's public key is not part of this shape — the fingerprint is the only part of it anybody has a use for.

status.description: `pending` means the machine has offered its key and is waiting for an operator. It runs nothing until it is approved.

online.description: A link is attached right now. An offline node's sandboxes are very likely still running; the control plane simply cannot reach them.

local.description: This gateway itself. It has no roster row, no fingerprint, and cannot be removed.

fingerprint.description: SHA256 of the machine's key — what an operator compares out of band before approving. Empty for this gateway.

sandboxes.description: Placements this machine still holds — across all owners, which is why this endpoint is operator-only.

Job.description: A long operation that outlived its request window. In memory only: a control-plane restart forgets it, because the restart also killed the work.

op.description: The operationId of the call that started it.

result.description: On success, exactly what the operation would have returned inline.

error.description: On failure, the same error object an inline failure carries.
